BREAKING: China’s central bank bought +8 tonnes of gold in April, the most since December 2024.

This follows +5 tonnes acquired in March, the 2nd-largest two-month addition since Q1 2024.

This also marks their 18th consecutive monthly purchase, bringing total official holdings up to a record 2,322 tonnes.

Year-to-date, China’s central bank has bought +15 tonnes of gold, on track for its biggest annual purchase since 2023.

Since 2022, the country has officially increased its gold holdings by +372 tonnes, or +19%, making China one of the strongest gold buyers in the world.

China is buying the dip in gold.

This has been a historic decade for markets:

The S&P 500 is on track for a 20% return in 2026, which would mark its 4th consecutive year of double-digit gains.

Since the start of 2023, the S&P 500 is now up a massive +93%.

If this happens, it would mark just the 2nd stretch of at least 4 consecutive years of double-digit annual returns since the index's debut in 1957.

The only other instance was the Dot-Com Bubble run, when the index rallied +20%+ for five consecutive years from 1995 to 1999.

Before that, the previous version of the index recorded 4 straight years of double-digit gains during World War II and the peace period that followed, from 1949 to 1952.

Market momentum is unlike anything markets have seen in decades.

Putting all of the above together, I get a most peculiar binary setup of two opposite tails, in wich we could easily get an AI-driven meltup in stocks, while at the same time being at risk of an oil crisis that feeds into all corners of the markets and the economy. What’s an investor to do? For one, rebalance! If we get the meltup, it wil be important to rebalance back to whatever your becnhmarks are. If the current oil shock goes from accuate to chronic, it will be critical to own assets that are negatively correlated (or at least uncorrelated) to both equities and bonds. Commodities, CTAs, cash, and Bitcoin are my current favorites.

Gold is a good long-term diversifier but currently it is positively correlated to bonds and as such, less likely to provide much protection. It now has been regularly going down on bad market days.

On that note, we can   see below that Bitcoin has been working off   its overbought condition in the most bullish way possible, by holding near   the recent highs rather than falling like a knife as would be common during   bear markets.

Bitcoin, on the other hand, has beenhanging in there like a champ as it has continued to steal the show from gold.
